notes: State of the art as reachable by API for ShoulderCut. status: implemented = wired in this repo today; available = callable with the configured fal key but not yet wired; planned = needs a new key, backend or product step. Rankings: Artificial Analysis video leaderboards, Oct 2026 snapshots. Prices are provider list indications, re-verify before spending.

techniques.name: Generated insert / from-scratch shot
techniques.task: Create a new shot that does not exist in the source footage, to cut into the edit or stand alone.
workflow: present result as a new clip

backends.price: fast tier, per-second; validation settings 480p/4s/no-audio in code
backends.ranking: Seedance family top group in text-to-video Elo
#1 text-to-video (1174) and #1 video editing (1198), no source-footage edit endpoint

risks: No continuity with adjacent real shots unless references are used
Native audio off in validation settings

techniques.name: Whole-frame instruction edit
techniques.task: Transform existing footage from a sentence, letting the model re-render the whole frame coherently (light, shadows, occlusions).
workflow: track_object(subject) when a subject is named
edit_segment or provider edit call with reference image
recomposite through dilated SAM mask locally

backends.ranking: outside editing top 9; element-based replacement is its strength

risks: Whole frame is regenerated: identity/background drift outside the target
Mitigate by local recomposite through a dilated, feathered mask (never the raw SAM edge)
techniques.economicalTest: Shorten segment to ~3 s around the action peak, lowest resolution tier, one attempt

techniques.name: Masked inpainting edit (native mask video)
techniques.task: Generate only inside a SAM mask video; everything outside is preserved by the model and again by our recomposite.
guidance: ControlNet-style control videos in the VACE family (depth/reframe endpoints)

backends.ranking: Wan 2.x generation; only shortlisted model with native mask-video input

risks: Weakest image quality of the shortlist (proven on the demo: timid transformation without reference + negative prompt)
Seams, and shadows/contacts outside the mask stay those of the original body: dilate the recomposite mask over shadow/contact zones
techniques.economicalTest: 81 frames at 16 fps, 480p, fixed seed (done on bedroom.mp4, ~$0.20)

techniques.name: Character replacement driven by the source motion
techniques.task: A new character re-performs the source footage: appearance comes from a character image, motion and scene integration from the source video.
workflow: track_object(subject) to bound the subject and build assets
build the character image (Muse Image or flux reference, or edited keyframe)
REFRAME the character image so the character occupies the same fraction of frame height as the subject in the source (SCAIL-2 rule: reference framing controls output scale)
provider character-replace call: SCAIL-2 (reference workflow) or fal Recast; NOT mask-inpainting
keep the provider raw output; do not mask-recomposite SCAIL/Recast output (halo, broken contact/occlusion)

backends.ranking: Purpose-built for this exact job and the current community/official reference: SAM3 tracking + SCAIL2ColoredMask (no pose skeleton), WanSCAILToVideo replacement_mode=true, pose_strength 1, lightx2v distill LoRA 0.8 + SCAIL DPO LoRA 1.0, ModelSamplingSD3 shift 5, euler/simple 6 steps CFG 1. Rules: reference framing controls output scale (reframe to subject frame-height fraction); describe the RESULT in the prompt, not an instruction; leave raw output un-composited. TESTED 2026-10-30 locally (RTX 4070 Ti 12GB, int8 template settings, 960x544, 65 frames, ~57 s/step, 6 steps): identity stable and background preserved, screen position/trajectory follow the source, but body orientation still drifts toward camera vs the side-profile source. Fidelity gain over Recast is position/scale, not orientation lock.

backends.price: $0.30/s at 768P, $0.45/s at 1080P; source 5-30 s, single shot <= 15 s
backends.ranking: TESTED 2026-10-29 on easy stock clip (woman walking on hill -> robot reference): robot identity stable across 5 s (grey metal body, orange joints, cyan eyes, antenna), scene and ground integration convincing, output 1344x768 24 fps. Caveat: the robot re-performs facing camera rather than keeping the exact side profile of the source walk. First backend that passes the visual bar for full character replacement. RETEST 2026-10-29 with hardened side-profile prompt: orientation NOT corrected (robot still performs facing camera). Prompt wording cannot fix performance fidelity on this backend; use SCAIL-2 for frame-tracked fidelity.

Tested 2026-10-29: ghostly/translucent result on real footage. Hosted endpoint exposes none of the ComfyUI WanVideoAnimateEmbeds tuning (pose_strength, face_strength, relight LoRA). Prefer SCAIL-2/Recast.

risks: One character per call in practice; two subjects may need two passes
Character image proportions drive the result: use a full-body, unoccluded reference
SCAIL-2: a full-bleed portrait reference against a wide shot renders the character oversized (measured 1.71x); reframe first
Mask-inpainting (VACE) is the wrong workflow for full character replacement: it repaints inside the source silhouette; reserve it for localised edits (garment, prop, removal)
techniques.economicalTest: 480p, shortest segment around the action peak, one character first

techniques.name: Keyframe-guided replacement (mask as production intermediate)
techniques.task: Edit the replacement into ONE frame with an image model under full control, then propagate that appearance through the shot with a video backend.
workflow: image-inpaint the keyframe (planned tool; today: external/Muse Image edit)
feed keyframe to character_replace_motion or instruction_video_edit as reference

backends.model: image inpainting (FLUX Fill class / Muse Image edits)
backends.ranking: Image inpainting is mask-native and far stronger per dollar than video frames

risks: Appearance drift over long shots; re-anchor with a second keyframe beyond ~5 s
Not yet wired as a single tool in this repo
techniques.economicalTest: One keyframe first; judge the still before any video spend

techniques.name: Motion transfer onto a character
techniques.task: A character image performs the movements of a separate reference video.

backends.ranking: Reference motion transfer, up to 30 s in video orientation

risks: Driver video should show a full or upper body, unobstructed
Generated scene, not the source footage: do not promise background preservation
techniques.economicalTest: Short driver excerpt, image orientation first

techniques.name: First/last-frame transition
techniques.task: Generate the in-between between an imposed start image and an imposed end image.
workflow: prepare both frames (frames of the edit or generated stills)
cut the result between the two shots

backends.ranking: Chosen for control surface, not Elo (text-to-video ~#21)
Hosted variants behind the same fal key

risks: In-between motion is invented: keep transitions short
Frames must share aspect and scale
techniques.economicalTest: Shortest duration tier, one transition only

techniques.name: Reference-bound generation (identity/elements)
techniques.task: Generate new footage where a person/product must persist across shots, bound by reference media.
guidance: reference images/videos addressed as @Image/@Element in the prompt
workflow: collect or generate the reference set
generate_shot with references (reference support planned in the tool)
reuse the same references for every shot of the sequence

backends.ranking: Up to 9 images + 3 videos + 3 audio references

risks: Identity holds best with clean, multi-angle references
Mixing providers mid-sequence breaks identity: one sequence, one backend
techniques.economicalTest: One hero shot first; validate identity before generating the sequence

techniques.name: Outpainting / reframing
techniques.task: Extend the frame beyond its borders (format change, camera widening) with generated surroundings.
workflow: grade-match borders with a shader pass if needed

backends.ranking: Same VACE family as the implemented inpainting

risks: Invented surroundings must stay generic (sky, wall, floor)
Fast camera moves expose border invention
techniques.economicalTest: Short segment, 480p, check borders on the fastest frame

techniques.name: Deterministic shader effect (no generation)
techniques.task: Anything expressible as pixels math over the real footage: grade, blur, particles, 3D overlay, titles, camera moves. Instant, free, frame-exact.
workflow: get_shader_interface if not read this session

backends.ranking: Real-time; the finishing layer for every generative result

risks: Cannot invent new photographed content
If the request needs new content, route to a generative technique instead of faking it
techniques.economicalTest: Always try this first when the request is a treatment, not new content
